source.title: Error Bounds of Supervised Classification from Information-Theoretic Perspective
source.authors: Binchuan Qi; Wei Gong; Li Li

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops bounds on fitting and expected risk and reports MNIST loss and risk curves. It does not measure training classification error or test any listed version’s training-error claim.
record.gate_note: The authors’ claims about overparameterization and gradient-based optimization are theoretical arguments. The MNIST experiments report loss and expected-risk trends, not training classification error. Their architectural comparison is recorded under fits_no_version because its risk measure does not match a version’s stated training-error measure.
record.test_reason: The study derives bounds on fitting error and expected risk and illustrates them with MNIST test-loss curves. It does not measure training classification error, depth-induced training degradation, spurious-minimum frequencies, initialization effects, learning-rate stability thresholds, or batch-normalization benefits. Its theoretical fitting error is the gap between empirical risk and model risk, not training classification error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive risk bounds involving gradients, parameter count, and classification uncertainty, interpret them as explanations of overparameterization, non-convex optimization, and flat minima, and report positive correspondence between their bound-related quantity and MNIST test risk.
record.recipe_differences: The paper derives information-theoretic bounds and illustrates risk and loss trends on MNIST; it does not reproduce the listed training-classification-error experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the residual-block model converges more rapidly but has larger expected risk than the standard model in the k=1 comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: For k=1 on MNIST, the authors report faster convergence for residual Model b but smaller expected risk for standard Model a.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this MNIST comparison, residual connections accelerate convergence while yielding a higher reported test/conditional risk.

fits_no_version.finding: Sections 7.1–7.2 argue that additional parameters can reduce a normalized fitting-error bound and that gradient-based optimization reduces its gradient-dependent component under the stated assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter count and stationary-point assumptions can control a bound on the discrepancy between empirical risk and model risk.

record.problems: The empirical section uses MNIST and reports one epoch of training. The architecture comparison's curves are figure-only, and the text provides no uncertainty estimates or classification training-error results.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also plots F and the difference between expected risk and F as depth k increases from 1 to 4 (Figures 2 and 3). These are bound-related quantities rather than the training-classification-error behavior named in the claim, so they are not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on capacity, training duration, and regularization.
Spurious local minima in ReLU teacher-student problems and their frequency with one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation across depth and its prevention by identity shortcuts; special initialization and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization-dependent training speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Loss and curvature dynamics relative to learning-rate stability thresholds, including recovery and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The depth-dependent risk-minus-F curves are already declared in rows_left_out. Neither those curves nor the fitting-error arguments establish the training behaviors named by V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; model size and training duration effects.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Training classification error across depth with and without identity shortcuts on ImageNet or CIFAR-10; special initializations and residual networks without normalization.
Initialization effects on training speed or trainable depth, including orthogonal and Gaussian weights.
Training outcomes and curvature behavior at learning rates above or near a stability limit.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.

rows.subject: Model a
rows.operation_detail: Trained the standard network on MNIST with cross-entropy loss.
rows.measure: Expected risk curve during training (reported as log2 Rℓ(fθ(x), q̄Y|x)).
rows.note: The text says the expected-risk and F trends remain entirely consistent as the model progresses toward convergence. Numerical values are only plotted.
rows.check: Section 8 describes test-loss changes and plots conditional risk for an arbitrary input x; the row should not imply a measured population-average risk. This measure cannot establish any listed version.

rows.subject: Model b
rows.operation_detail: Trained the network with residual blocks on MNIST with cross-entropy loss.

conditions.value: network incorporating residual blocks, Model b

rows.measure: Expected risk curve during training (reported as log2 Rℓ(fθ(x), q̄Y|x)).
rows.baseline: Model a has a smaller expected risk; exact value not stated
rows.note: The text says Model b converges more rapidly, but Model a achieves a smaller expected risk. Numerical values are only plotted.
rows.check: The reported faster convergence and larger test/conditional risk concern the k=1 residual model. They do not measure training-error degradation across depths or its prevention by shortcuts. As in R1, population-average risk is not established.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
